chunks.text: Ocean Forest Ecolodge — A Wellness Sanctuary on Costa Rica's Osa Peninsula Ocean Forest Ecolodge · Costa Rica Stay Wellness About Reserve Osa Peninsula · Costa Rica A sanctuary at the edge of the world.  We are a small wellness ecolodge on a roadless beach in the Osa Peninsula.  Ten rooms, one mile of sand, and the quiet that only comes when there is no other way to arrive but by boat.  Plan your stay Our wellness programs A note from the lodge We built this place slowly, the way the forest builds itself.  A cabin first, then a path, then a garden, then a kitchen, then — over many seasons — a small community that learned how to live here without needing very much.  You'll find ten rooms scattered into the trees, a three-storey wooden lodge we call Lapa Lapa, and a dharma hall on its ground floor where we gather most mornings.

chunks.title: index
chunks.text: You'll also find us — the people who make breakfast, who walk the turtle patrols, who can tell you which fruit is ripe today.  If you are looking for somewhere to rest, to practise, to remember the shape of your own thinking — we would love to have you.  Write to us.  We answer every letter ourselves.  Get in touch Scarlet macaws Spider monkeys Humpback whales Olive ridley turtles Toucans Spinner dolphins What you'll find here A sanctuary, a beach, a way of living.  Wellness The Dharma Hall A 150-square-metre open-air practice hall on the ground floor of Lapa Lapa, where we host yoga, breathwork, sound, and plant medicine retreats year-round.  Our programs Stay Ten rooms in the trees Hand-built cabins and bungalows for thirty guests, with three garden meals a day, hammocks on every veranda, and the surf ten paces away.

chunks.title: index
chunks.text: See the lodge Mission Built around the forest Sixteen years of marine turtle patrols.  A 15-acre ethnobotanical garden.  A lodge that is off-grid by design and run mostly by neighbours.  Our story The beach A mile of sand, between sea and forest.  San Josecito Beach runs in a long honey-coloured curve between two headlands of primary rainforest.  There are no other lodges, no roads, no electricity past ours.  You arrive by a small boat from Sierpe — a slow, hour-and-a-half journey through Central America's largest mangrove forest, past monkeys, caimans, and birds you'll start naming by the end of the week.  The Pacific is warm, the surf is gentle most days, and we keep kayaks and snorkel gear at the lodge for whenever the mood takes you.  Wellness A place to practise — and to land.  The Dharma Hall opens onto the garden.

chunks.title: index
chunks.text: We host our own seasonal retreats here — yoga, breathwork, plant medicine, ethnobotany — and welcome a small number of visiting teachers each year for full-property retreats up to thirty guests.  Whether you come for a programme or simply to be still, the lodge gives you the conditions: warm climate, real food, a forest that does most of the work for you.  Explore wellness Glimpses The Osa, in fragments.  From a recent guest It is the rarest thing — a place that has actually become more wild because people came to live in it.  The garden gives, the forest receives, and somewhere between the two you remember how it is supposed to feel to be alive.  — A guest, recent stay Come stay with us.  We answer every reservation personally.  Tell us a little about you, and we'll find a way.

chunks.title: accommodations
chunks.text: The Lodge — Ten Rooms in the Trees | Ocean Forest Ecolodge Ocean Forest Ecolodge · Costa Rica Stay Wellness About Reserve The Lodge Ten rooms beneath the canopy.  A three-storey wooden lodge and a handful of cabins scattered into the garden — built by hand from reclaimed hardwoods and bamboo, off-grid, naturally cooled, and a few steps from the surf.  The first thing you'll notice is the silence — and then, the absence of silence: the surf, the cicadas, the howler monkeys at dawn.  We built the Lapa Lapa Lodge, our three-storey timber building, fourteen metres into the canopy without taking down a single mature tree.  Around it sit our ten cabins and bungalows, far enough apart that you'll hear your neighbour's wind chime but not their conversation.  The whole place was designed for thirty guests.  That's the limit, even on our busiest weeks.  We like it that way.

chunks.title: accommodations
chunks.text: Where you'll sleep Three kinds of room, one kind of quiet.  Every room has an en-suite bathroom with hot water, a ceiling fan, a memory-foam bed under mosquito netting, and a private veranda or terrace with a hammock.  Wi-Fi works at the main lodge — we keep it light on purpose.  2 guests Garden View Garden Bungalow Tucked into the ethnobotanical garden, ten metres from the breakfast hall.  King bed, private veranda with hammock, outdoor rinse shower for after the beach.  Enquire 2 guests Ocean View Ocean Cabin On the rise above the beach, with a wide deck angled at the Pacific.  Whale-watching from your hammock between June and December, if you're lucky.  Enquire 4 guests Family Lapa Family Suite A two-room suite on the second floor of the main lodge.  Two queens or a king plus two singles, two bathrooms, and the largest balcony on the property.

chunks.title: accommodations
chunks.text: Enquire Rates include three garden meals daily, complimentary cacao, tea and coffee, kayaks and snorkel gear, and the daily naturalist walk.  Write to us for current rates.  Lapa Lapa Lodge A three-storey lodge built by hand.  The main lodge is the heart of the property — three floors of open-air timber rising fourteen metres into the trees, every column a fallen hardwood, every joint hand-cut.  The Dharma Hall is on the ground floor: a hundred-and-fifty-square-metre practice space where we host yoga, breathwork, council and ceremony.  Above it, a library and reading lounge full of hammocks and field guides.  Above that, our family suite and a wide open deck where most of the lodge's morning life happens — guests, staff, the occasional toucan in the rafters.  The Dharma Hall & programs The Kitchen Three meals a day, mostly from the garden.  Our kitchen cooks around the seasons.

chunks.title: accommodations
chunks.text: Mornings open with slow oats and pineapple, tropical fruit salads of fresh mango and papaya, eggs from our hens, and ceremonial cacao.  Lunches lean light — gazpachos, ceviches of plantain and hearts of palm, garden salads.  Dinner is the long table: baked chicken in coconut milk, curried vegetables with wild-harvested turmeric and ginger, line-caught Pacific fish, whole-grain rice from the mountain neighbours.  We're happy to cook around any diet — vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, allergies — just tell us when you book.  How we run the place Light footprint, by design.  Energy Solar & micro-hydro Off-grid from day one.  A hybrid solar array and a small upstream micro-hydro turbine power the whole property.  Water Mountain spring Drinking water comes from a protected spring on the property, gravity-fed and filtered.  Rainwater feeds the gardens.

chunks.title: accommodations
chunks.text: Materials Reclaimed timber Every structure is reclaimed hardwood, bamboo and river stone.  No old-growth tree was felled for the lodge.  Food Mostly grown here About seventy percent of what arrives at the table comes from the property; the rest from neighbour farms within ten kilometres.  Getting here It's meant to be a journey.  Reaching us from San José takes most of a morning, on purpose.  We can arrange every leg.  By air Daily 50-minute flights from San José (SJO) into Drake Bay (DRK).  We meet you at the airstrip.  By boat from Sierpe The classic approach — a 1. 5-hour boat ride through Central America's largest mangrove forest, where you'll likely see monkeys, caimans and dozens of birds before you arrive.  The last mile From Drake Bay to the lodge there is no road — only a short boat transfer along the coast.  We handle it.

chunks.title: wellness
chunks.text: Wellness — The Dharma Hall & Retreats | Ocean Forest Ecolodge Ocean Forest Ecolodge · Costa Rica Stay Wellness About Reserve Wellness A place to practise.  A place to land.  The Dharma Hall opens onto the garden.  We host our own seasonal retreats here, and welcome a small number of visiting teachers each year — yoga, breathwork, sound, plant medicine, and the slow work of paying attention.  We didn't set out to build a retreat centre.  The Dharma Hall came later — when enough teachers had visited the lodge and asked if there was somewhere they could hold a circle, run a week of yoga, sit a longer practice.  So we built one.  It's a hundred-and-fifty square metres of open-air floor on the ground level of Lapa Lapa, framed by hardwood columns, with the garden on one side and the path to the beach on the other.  Most days it begins quietly at dawn and ends quietly at dusk.

chunks.title: about
chunks.text: About — Our Story, Our Mission | Ocean Forest Ecolodge Ocean Forest Ecolodge · Costa Rica Stay Wellness About Reserve About the lodge The reason we're here.  We built the lodge so that the work could exist.  Sixteen years of marine turtle patrols, a fifteen-acre ethnobotanical garden, an off-grid property — all of it held together by guests who come to rest, and a community that comes back each season.  Our story We came to this beach a long time ago, looking for a way to live in close relationship to a rainforest that did not need us.  The peninsula was already changing — too many roads being cut, too many fences going up, too many old neighbours quietly leaving.  We thought: if we could build something small here, and run it gently, we could pay for the work the forest needs us to do.  That's still the answer to most questions about the lodge.  Why ten rooms and not forty?

chunks.title: about
chunks.text: Because thirty guests is the limit of what this beach can support without changing.  Why no road?  Because the road would change everything.  Why three meals a day from the garden?  Because we'd rather grow the food than ship it.  We are a small team.  Most of us live here year-round, on the property or in the village next door.  Twenty-three of our twenty-five staff are from Drake Bay, Agujitas or the surrounding hills.  The lodge is run on solar power, the water comes from a mountain spring on the back of the land, and the food is mostly grown a hundred metres from your fork.  None of this is unusual any more.  It's just how we built it.  Three programmes What every stay funds.  A portion of every reservation goes directly into one of three year-round programmes.  They are the slow, accumulating work that keeps this corner of the Osa intact.

chunks.title: about
chunks.text: Marine Marine turtle patrols Sixteen consecutive years, in partnership with Fundación Corcovado and Fundación Osa.  Olive ridley, Pacific green and (rarely) hawksbill turtles all nest on the beach in front of the lodge.  Botanical The ethnobotanical garden Fifteen acres above the lodge, curated with the Universidad de Costa Rica.  Three hundred and fifty species of fruit, medicine, herb and tree from across the tropical Americas and Asia.  Forest Forest & community We work with the Asociación de Productores de Drake to maintain forest cover on neighbouring smallholdings, and run a year-round environmental literacy programme in the village schools.  Sixteen years on the night beach The work we are proudest of.  Every nesting season, our team walks a 1. 6-kilometre stretch of San Josecito Beach by night, looking for the broken-bicycle track that means a female turtle has come ashore.

chunks.title: about
chunks.text: We relocate vulnerable nests to a protected hatchery, monitor temperatures, and release hatchlings at dawn.  The data we collect feeds national monitoring and international IUCN reporting.  We've grown the hatchery slowly over sixteen consecutive years, and we run it under permit from Costa Rica's Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía.  Guests are welcome to join a patrol or release in season — write to us. Fifteen acres on the rise above the lodge, planted plant by plant.  Cacao trees, fruit orchards, aromatic herbs, medicinal bitters, adaptogens, vanilla orchids climbing the older guapinols.  Many of the cuttings came from elders across Mesoamerica.  A daily naturalist walk is open to every guest.

chunks.title: Ocean Forest Ecolodge — Concierge Knowledge
chunks.text: Edit this file whenever rates, policies, or seasonal details change. Redeploy the site to update the concierge.

chunks.title: Rates & availability
chunks.text:
Current room rates are **on request** — the concierge must not invent prices. Direct guests to complete an enquiry and the team will reply within 24 hours (usually sooner) with current rates and availability.

Rates include three garden meals daily, complimentary cacao, tea and coffee, kayaks and snorkel gear, and the daily naturalist walk.

The lodge has **ten rooms** and a maximum of **thirty guests** at any time, even on busy weeks.

chunks.title: Food
chunks.text:
Three meals a day are included. The kitchen uses fresh local Costa Rican produce and ingredients sourced from the region. Meals are omnivore — meat, fish, and plant-based options are all part of the kitchen's repertoire. Cooking is done by local women from the area, and the food reflects the place: seasonal, fresh, grounded.

Vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, and allergy accommodations are available — guests should mention dietary needs when booking.

Cacao ceremonies are available on request — enquire with the team when booking.

chunks.title: Room recommendations
chunks.text:
**Garden Bungalow** (2 guests): Best for couples who want to be close to the garden and breakfast hall. Quiet, ten metres from the kitchen. Outdoor rinse shower after the beach.

**Ocean Cabin** (2 guests): Best for couples who want Pacific views and whale-watching from the deck (June–December). On the rise above the beach.

**Lapa Family Suite** (4 guests): Best for families or small groups. Two-room suite on the second floor of the main lodge. Two queens or king plus two singles, two bathrooms, largest balcony on the property.

Every room includes en-suite bathroom with hot water, ceiling fan, memory-foam bed under mosquito netting, and private veranda or terrace with hammock.

chunks.title: Daily activities & yoga
chunks.text:
All guests have access to a daily **Budokon yoga class** held in the Dharma Hall — this is not retreat-only. Budokon is a martial arts-inspired movement practice combining yoga, mobility, and bodyweight strength. All levels welcome.

Also included for all guests: kayaks, snorkel gear, beach access, and the daily naturalist walk at 9:30am through the ethnobotanical garden.

chunks.title: Excursions & adventures
chunks.text:
The lodge organises all excursions directly — guests don't need to find their own operators. Excursion costs are not included in the room rate; each excursion is approximately **$100 per person**.

**Caño Island Biological Reserve:** One of the best snorkeling and diving spots in Costa Rica, with abundant marine life. A highlight for many guests. Bookable through the lodge.

**Corcovado National Park:** Day trips into one of the most biodiverse parks on Earth. The lodge arranges guides and logistics.

All other adventures in the area follow the same model — the team handles the planning, guests just show up. Ask about current options when enquiring or at check-in.

chunks.title: Retreats
chunks.text:
The Dharma Hall is 150 m² open-air practice space on the ground floor of Lapa Lapa Lodge. Holds up to 30 practitioners.

Retreat types hosted: Yoga & Pranayama, Cacao & Council Circles, Plants People & Place (ethnobotany), Sound Bath & Silent Retreats, Permaculture Design, Writing & Watercolour.

Upcoming retreat dates are shared by email — the concierge should not invent specific dates. Offer to capture an enquiry and the team will share the wait-list.

Whole-property buyouts available for groups of 22–30 across all ten rooms.

chunks.title: Policies
chunks.text:
**Currency:** USD and Costa Rican colones accepted. Major cards welcome.

**Cancellation:** Full refund up to 30 days before arrival. Exceptions made when life intervenes — guests should write to the team.

**Travel insurance:** Strongly recommended. The team can suggest local providers.

**Deposit:** Contact the team for current deposit requirements — do not guess amounts.

**Check-in / check-out:** Check-in after 12:00pm. Check-out before 10:00am.

**Minimum stay:** 2 nights.

**Children:** The lodge does not host children. Ocean Forest is designed for adults.

**Pets:** Not permitted.

**Solo travelers:** Very welcome. The lodge is a great fit for solo guests — the community feel, shared meals, and daily activities make it easy to connect with other guests and staff.

**Accessibility:** The lodge's remote rainforest and beach setting involves uneven terrain, boat transfers, and natural paths. It is not suited for guests with significant mobility limitations. Contact the team if you have specific questions.

chunks.title: Arrival & logistics
chunks.text:
**On arrival:** A member of the team meets every guest at the airstrip or boat dock. There is a welcome orientation and drink on arrival. The transition from travel to the lodge is looked after.

**Boat transfer from Drake Bay:** Included in the stay. The lodge handles all coastal transfers — guests don't arrange this themselves.

**If you miss the boat or arrive late:** The team will arrange drivers to get you there. Don't panic — contact the lodge directly.

**Mobile signal:** There is no mobile phone signal at the lodge. There is Wi-Fi at the main lodge building.

**Laundry:** Available on-site.

chunks.title: Safety & nature
chunks.text:
**Swimming:** San Josecito Beach is safe and beautiful for swimming. Clean open water.

**Wildlife & insects:** The Osa Peninsula is wild — insects are part of the experience. The lodge provides mosquito netting on all beds. Bring repellent. The area is home to snakes and other wildlife, but the lodge has clear protocols and guests are briefed on arrival. Thousands of visitors come through safely each year.

**Medical:** In the event of a medical need, Drake Bay village has a hospital. The team knows the local emergency procedures and will assist.

chunks.title: About the lodge
chunks.text: Ocean Forest Ecolodge is owned and stewarded by **Jonathon**. The lodge runs on solar and micro-hydro power and is built on permaculture principles. The Lapa Lapa Lodge — the three-story main building — was constructed entirely from sustainably sourced and reclaimed materials with no living trees cut. It is an ecolodge in the full sense of the word, not a resort.

chunks.title: Seasonal notes
chunks.text:
**Dry season (roughly December–April):** Sunniest months, popular for travel. Book early.

**Green season (roughly May–November):** Afternoon rains, lush forest, fewer crowds. Mornings are often clear. Turtle nesting season runs roughly July–December on San Josecito Beach.

**Whale watching:** Humpback whales pass offshore June–December — best viewed from Ocean Cabins.

**Turtle patrols:** Guests may join night patrols or dawn hatchling releases in nesting season — enquire when booking.

chunks.title: Location
chunks.text:
Ocean Forest Ecolodge sits on **San Josecito Beach**, south of **Drake Bay (Agujitas)**, on Costa Rica's **Osa Peninsula** — one of the most biodiverse regions on Earth. Coordinates: 8°41'N 83°41'W.

There are **no roads** to the lodge. The last leg is always a short **coastal boat transfer** from Drake Bay village or the airstrip.

chunks.title: Getting there
chunks.text:
### From San José (SJO)

1. **Fly:** Daily ~50-minute flights from San José (SJO) to Drake Bay (DRK). The lodge meets guests at the airstrip.
2. **Boat from Sierpe:** Classic approach — ~1.5-hour boat through Central America's largest mangrove forest. Wildlife sightings common (monkeys, caimans, birds).
3. **Last mile:** From Drake Bay to the lodge — ~20-minute coastal boat transfer. The lodge handles this.

The lodge can arrange every leg of the journey — mention this when guests ask about logistics.

### Travel times (approximate)

| Leg | Duration |
|-----|----------|
| SJO → DRK (flight) | ~50 minutes |
| Sierpe → lodge (mangrove boat) | ~1.5 hours |
| Drake Bay → lodge (coastal transfer) | ~20 minutes |

Reaching the lodge from San José takes most of a morning — by design.

chunks.title: Climate & seasons
chunks.text:
**Tropical rainforest climate.** Warm year-round (typically 24–32°C / 75–90°F).

**Dry season (Dec–Apr):** Less rain, sunnier skies. Peak travel season.

**Green / rainy season (May–Nov):** Afternoon showers, vibrant forest. Mornings often clear. Lower crowds.

**Humidity:** High year-round. Light, breathable clothing recommended.

chunks.title: What to pack
chunks.text:
- Lightweight long sleeves and pants (sun + insects)
- Rain jacket or poncho (green season)
- Sturdy sandals and closed shoes for walks
- Reef-safe sunscreen and hat
- Insect repellent (natural options welcome)
- Swimsuit — beach and kayaks on-site
- Binoculars for wildlife
- Headlamp (for turtle patrols in season)
- Reusable water bottle (refill stations on-site)
- Any medications — nearest pharmacy is in Drake Bay village

Wi-Fi works at the main lodge only — kept intentionally light.

chunks.title: Wildlife & nature
chunks.text:
The Osa Peninsula hosts scarlet macaws, toucans, howler monkeys, sloths, dolphins, whales (Jun–Dec), and three species of nesting sea turtles on San Josecito Beach (olive ridley, Pacific green, rarely hawksbill).

**Daily naturalist walk:** 9:30am through the ethnobotanical garden, ends with a tasting in the kitchen. Included for all guests.

**On-site activities (included):** Kayaks, snorkel gear, daily naturalist walk, beach access.

chunks.title: Nearby
chunks.text:
**Drake Bay village (Agujitas):** Small village with basic shops, pharmacy, restaurants. Accessible by boat.

**Corcovado National Park:** One of Costa Rica's premier wilderness areas — day trips can be arranged; enquire with the lodge team.

**Sierpe:** Gateway town for the mangrove boat route; mangrove tours are a highlight of the journey itself.

chunks.title: Practical tips
chunks.text:
